title: [D1 Ingest] Per-format adapter interface
summary: `helena.normalizer` now reads its input through an adapter selected by `HELENA_INPUT_FORMAT`: `parse(line: bytes) -> FlowRecord | ParseFailure`, with no capture, no identity and no configuration, so an adapter cannot stamp a tenant, decide an event id or add a field to the event. Two are registered — `flow-json`, the format every real capture is in, and `flow-envelope`, a deliberately trivial synthetic second format — and a refused record now comes back as a typed `ParseFailure` (`malformed_json` / `not_this_format` / `contract_violation`) rather than as an exception, so a bad record does not stall the capture. 89 new tests; the suite is 396 passed.
assumption_validated: That a second input format can be absorbed by writing an adapter and changing a configuration value, with no change to the normalized event contract. Positive, and measured rather than asserted: the same ten records exist in two capture files in two formats, are read by two adapters selected by `HELENA_INPUT_FORMAT` alone, and produce `NormalizedEvent`s whose observations are equal field for field and whose stamped `schema_version` is the same one (the event ids differ, and must — two files are two captures, so two raw-record references). The complementary half is structural: no model reachable from `NormalizedEvent` has a field naming a format, an adapter or a parse failure, so a third format cannot be accommodated by quietly adding one. A negative result worth recording alongside it: the `not_this_format` reason is NOT symmetric between the two formats — only a format that declares itself can report it, so an envelope line reaching the flat adapter is indistinguishable from producer drift and comes back as `contract_violation`. Measured and pinned by a test rather than claimed away. And the honest limit of the whole demonstration: `flow-envelope` renames and re-nests, so it proves the boundary holds for a format the contract can already express — it says nothing about a format carrying something `FlowRecord` has no place for.
makes_buildable: Task 9 (quarantine) has the typed value to route and store: `ParseFailure{input_format, reason, detail}` with a three-reason closed vocabulary that must stay distinct in the table and in the counter, plus the `RawRecordReference` the caller pairs with it (`normalize` returns a failure for the record it was given; `normalize_capture` yields exactly one result per record in file order, so `enumerate` gives the offset for both outcomes). The quarantine rate it exposes now has three numerators that mean different things. Task 10 (broker wiring) has the one parse path both ingress and replay must use — `Normalizer.from_settings(settings)` resolves the adapter from configuration, so the consumer cannot pick a different one — and `normalize_capture`'s one-result-per-record guarantee is what makes consumed-versus-normalized-versus-quarantined reconcile against `Capture.record_count`. Task 11 (replay driver) inherits the same: replay reads through the configured adapter or it is a parallel path. Anything adding a third format now knows the shape: an adapter class, an entry in `INPUT_ADAPTERS`, and a value in `HELENA_INPUT_FORMAT`.

verification.detail: 396 passed in 14.0 s, no skips (was 307; 89 new tests). `uv lock --check` clean, compileall clean, no new dependency. `uv run pytest -q -m integration` separately confirms the 15 engine-backed tests really executed against a RisingWave instance rather than skipping. No SQL was added by this task — nothing stores an event or a parse failure yet — so there was no new SQL to execute. Four mutation checks were run against the new tests before believing them, each restored afterwards: (1) removing the `layers`-shadowing guard from the envelope adapter fails the shadowing case; (2) swapping the envelope's `start`/`duration` mapping fails the cross-format observation-equality test while correctly leaving the fixture-derivation test green, because that test carries its own transform; (3) adding an `input_format` field to `EventIdentity` fails both the no-format-on-the-event test and the no-defaults test; (4) the parse-failure vocabulary was measured against Pydantic 2.13 first (`json_invalid` vs `model_type` vs `extra_forbidden`/`missing`) rather than assumed. Line length checked with `awk 'length>88'`; the only over-length lines left are the three pre-existing ones task 7 recorded.

escalations.detail: One new configuration variable, `HELENA_INPUT_FORMAT`, required and without a default, added to `helena.config.REQUIRED_VARIABLES`, `.env.example`, the local `.env` (value `flow-json`) and ADR-0004. It is not on `concept/instruction.md` §3's escalation list — it is not a dependency, a store, an enrichment source, a contract field or an egress channel — and the task's own step 5 asks for adding an adapter to be a configuration change, so it was made rather than escalated. Recorded here because it changes what a deployment must set: an existing `.env` without it now fails at startup naming the variable, which is the intended direction.

No contract field was added or changed — that is the point of the task, and a test asserts it. Recorded as a non-escalation so the next session does not go looking: `NormalizedEvent` is still `{identity, observation}` and `EventIdentity` still the same five fields.

invariant_conflicts.step: Define the adapter protocol: raw bytes/line in, validated normalized event or typed parse failure out
invariant_conflicts.detail: The adapter returns the validated OBSERVATION (`FlowRecord`), not a `NormalizedEvent`. Identity is assigned in exactly one place from deployment configuration (ADR-0011, `concept/02-concepts-and-taxonomy.md`), and an adapter that could assemble an identity would be one more place a tenant could come from — one per format, each able to get it wrong silently, which is `concept/instruction.md` §6's defaulted tenant. The step's stated shape still holds one level up: `Normalizer.normalize(capture, offset, line)` is bytes in, a validated normalized event or a typed parse failure out. Narrowing the adapter is what keeps that true for every future format.
invariant_conflicts.resolution: Narrowed rather than skipped; recorded in docs/decisions/0012 and pinned by the test that the event contract has no place for a format.

invariant_conflicts.step: Implement a deliberately trivial second adapter over a variant fixture format
invariant_conflicts.detail: Not a conflict but a tension with `concept/instruction.md` §1 — *no interface with one implementation, no registry for two things*. The second adapter is precisely what stops this from being a speculative abstraction: without it the boundary claim in `concept/06-technology.md` and `concept/07-principles.md` is untested and the interface is a shape nobody pushed against. It is recorded because the cost is real: `flow-envelope` is synthetic, no producer sends it, and it must be labelled that way wherever it appears so nobody later reads it as a supported input. It is so labelled in the module, in ADR-0012 and in the fixture README.
invariant_conflicts.resolution: Built, and labelled synthetic in every place it is named.

deferred: Storing and counting parse failures — the definition-of-done item that says a new failure path is typed, STORED and countable. It is typed and it is impossible to drop silently (every record yields exactly one result, and a failure is a value the caller must handle), but nothing writes it anywhere and no counter exists. That is task 9's quarantine table and quarantine-rate counter in as many words, and inventing a table here would be writing task 9's contract ahead of it. This is the one DoD item this increment does not satisfy on its own, and it is deferred by the PRD's own sequencing rather than by choice.

An adapter version on `ParseFailure`. Nothing stores or cites a parse failure yet, so a version on it would have one home and no reader; the increment that writes the quarantine row is where it belongs, beside the version set it stamps. Noted in ADR-0012 so it is not forgotten rather than left implicit.

Recording on a stored event which format it was read from. The event contract deliberately has no such field, and a test asserts it. The consequence is stated rather than hidden: re-deriving an event from a retained capture requires knowing that capture's format, which today is the deployment's configuration and nothing else. If a stored event ever needs to say it, that is a contract change and a decision.

Format sniffing, and more than one adapter per deployment. One adapter per deployment is deliberate: sniffing would make 'which parser produced this row' a property of the row rather than of the configuration, and a record that parsed as two formats would be resolved by whichever adapter was tried first. For the same reason a capture directory holds one format.
Streaming or chunked parsing. An adapter takes one whole line; `read_capture` still materialises the file (task 6's deferral, unchanged).
Any logging. Nothing here logs, for the same reason as task 7: there is no ingest run to attribute a line to.
lessons: task 08: Pydantic reports 'not JSON at all' and 'JSON, but not an object' as the same kind of `ValidationError` — measured on 2.13: `b'not json'` and a truncated line give `json_invalid`, while `b'[1,2]'`, `b'"x"'`, `b'12'` and `b'null'` all give `model_type`. `model_validate_json` therefore cannot keep the two apart without inspecting error types and locations. Decoding with `json.loads` first and validating the dict with `model_validate` keeps them apart structurally, and task 6's measurement that strict mode behaves identically for JSON input and Python objects is what makes the swap safe.

task 08: Invalid UTF-8 in a line raises `UnicodeDecodeError` from `json.loads`, not `json.JSONDecodeError` — both are `ValueError` subclasses but only one is caught if you catch `JSONDecodeError` alone. `b'{"id":"\xff"}'` is the case.

task 08: `tests/test_config.py::test_no_settings_field_has_a_default` iterated `Settings.model_fields[*].annotation` assuming every one is a `BaseModel`. The first scalar field on `Settings` (`input_format`) broke it with `AttributeError: type object 'str' has no attribute 'model_fields'`. Fixed by filtering the nested list to actual models; `Settings` itself is already in the list, so a scalar field is still checked.

task 08: A capture fixture directory now holds exactly one input format, and the second format's fixture lives in `tests/fixtures/captures-flow-envelope/`. This is load-bearing for the test suite, not only tidiness: `FIXTURE_LINES` in `tests/test_normalizer.py` sweeps every record of every capture in `tests/fixtures/captures/` and parses each as a `FlowRecord`, so a second-format file dropped in there would fail a dozen contract tests at once.

task 08: `_contract_models()` in the test suite now takes a root and still defaults to `FlowRecord`. Walking it from `NormalizedEvent` is what the new no-format-on-the-event test does, and task 7's warning still stands for the absence tests: they must keep walking from `FlowRecord` or the identity block sweeps in and fails every one.

task 08: A registry of two adapters keyed by name only earns its place because each adapter carries its own `input_format` and a test asserts key and attribute agree. Without that the dict is two places a format name can live.
failed_approaches: task 08: Putting the raw-record reference (capture digest plus offset) on `ParseFailure` was considered and rejected before it was written. It would make the adapter — which has no capture — either take a reference it does not use or hand back a narrower object the normalizer widens, i.e. two types for one thing. `normalize_capture` yields exactly one result per record in file order, so `enumerate` already gives a failure its offset, and an event carries its own.

task 08: Rendering `ParseFailure.detail` from `str(ValidationError)` was considered and rejected: Pydantic echoes the rejected input into the message, so the detail would carry a second uncontrolled copy of input the module has just refused to trust, and a fully-invalid record would produce an unbounded string with no visible truncation point. The detail is `loc: msg [type]` per error, and the raw record is kept exactly as read by whatever quarantines it. A test asserts a distinctive bad value does not appear in the detail while the field name does.

task 08: Making `flow-envelope` a pure passthrough wrapper (`{"flow": {…}}`) was considered and rejected as too weak: an adapter that does nothing but unwrap demonstrates registration but not that an adapter can map a differently-shaped record onto the same contract. It renames three scalars and re-nests the layers instead — still trivial, and it fails the cross-format equality test if the mapping is wrong (mutation-checked).

task 08: Merging the envelope's `layers` over the mapped scalars without a collision check was rejected: a `layers` key named `id` would silently replace the record's own id (or be silently dropped, depending on merge order), which is exactly the coercion the contract refuses everywhere else. A key collision is `not_this_format`, and removing that guard fails a test.
next_session_should_know: Parse input through `Normalizer.from_settings(settings)` and nothing else — the adapter comes from `HELENA_INPUT_FORMAT` and constructing a `Normalizer` by hand now needs `adapter=` as well as `identity=`. Six things that will bite otherwise. (1) `normalize` NO LONGER RAISES on a bad record: it returns `NormalizedEvent | ParseFailure`, and so does every element `normalize_capture` yields. Code that assumes an event will happily read `.identity` off a failure — `isinstance(result, ParseFailure)` is the check, and `enumerate` over `normalize_capture` gives each result its offset because there is exactly one result per record in file order. `normalize` still RAISES `CaptureError` for an offset that addresses no record; that is this deployment's bug, not input drift, and quarantining it would file a producer's name against our own mistake. (2) `HELENA_INPUT_FORMAT` is a new required variable. It is in the local `.env` as `flow-json`, in `.env.example` and in `helena.config.REQUIRED_VARIABLES`; an environment without it fails at startup naming it. `helena.config` does not validate the value — `helena.normalizer.adapter_for` does, raising `ConfigurationError` naming the variable and listing the registered formats. (3) The three parse-failure reasons must stay distinct all the way into task 9's table and counter: `malformed_json` (framing broke), `not_this_format` (wrong adapter configured), `contract_violation` (producer drift — the rate ADR-0010 says to watch). They are not equally precise: `flow-json` cannot report `not_this_format` for another format's JSON object because it has no envelope to check, and a test pins that asymmetry. (4) Adding a third input format is an adapter class, an entry in `INPUT_ADAPTERS` and a configuration value — never a contract change, and a test asserts the event contract has no field naming a format. If a format ever needs one, that is an escalation. (5) `tests/fixtures/captures/` is `flow-json` only; the second format's fixture is in `tests/fixtures/captures-flow-envelope/` and dropping a non-`flow-json` file into the first directory fails a dozen contract tests, because `FIXTURE_LINES` sweeps it. `flow-envelope` is synthetic — nothing sends it, it exists so the boundary claim is measured — and it should keep that label wherever it is mentioned. (6) Still true from task 7 and unchanged: no engine table holds an event, `EVENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` still has one home and needs its SQL copy plus equality test in the increment that first stores an event, capture identity is provisional under live ingestion (ADR-0010), and there is still no git repository, so nothing here was committed. `bin/README.md` still points at a `scripts/build-binaries.sh` that does not exist.
